description.narrative: Delivery of sanitation services by PPUC improved.

Treatment system outflow from the discharge pipe in Koror and Airai consistently meets EQPB standards and discharge consent requirements (2018 baseline: 0%) OP3.3.2 Progress/Status: The EQPB effluent discharge consent requirements for the Malakal WWTP, constructed under the project, are biochemical oxygen demand (BOD5)- 30mg/l, total nitrogen (TN) - 10mg/l, total phosphorus (TP) - 10mg/l, and total suspended solids (TSS) - 30mg/l. The level of compliance of the Malakal WWTP effluent with the EQPB consent requirements in 2024 was: BOD5 - 95% of samples (91 samples); TN - 71% (163 samples); TP - 100% (152 samples); and TSS - 87% (100 samples). Full compliance with the EQPB effluent discharge consent requirements was not achieved in 2024 due to mechanical failures in the WWTP's desludging system which resulted in degraded effluent quality for the last 4 months of 2024. The desludging system maintenance issues were addressed and PPUC staff training in belt press (sludge dewatering system) maintenance was conducted in December 2024. Additionally, the blowers installed for the WWTP aeration system when the plant was constructed were undersized and could not provide sufficient oxygen for the plant nutrient removal process. The original blowers were replaced with higher capacity blowers in March 2025 and the WWTP aeration requirements are now being fully met. ADB is providing the services of a process specialist to assist PPUC to improve the plant performance. Data Source: PPUC reported data Actual value:

Sewer overflows to the land and sea reported to EQPB reduced to 12 or fewer per year (2018 baseline: 25) OP3.3.1 Progress/Status: The number of sewer overflows decreased by more than 67% from 25 in 2018 to 8 in 2023. The decline in the frequency of sewer overflows is attributed to improved operations and maintenance of the sewer system by PPUC's Water and Wastewater Operations (WWO). Reduction in overflows that will result from new sewers constructed under the project have not yet been realized as the new sewers have yet to be connected and brought into service. The existing sewer pipe network is in poor condition and has substantial inflow and infiltration (I/I) of groundwater into sewers and a significant number of illegal stormwater connections. I/I may contribute up to 25% of sewer flows during dry weather and more than 50% during wet weather. When the new sewers are commissioned, further reductions in the frequency of overflows are expected as inflow and infiltration will be substantially reduced. Data Source: PPUC reported data Actual value:

Output: Safe and hygienic public toilet facilities in Koror are constructed Indicator: Newly constructed or rehabilitated facilities have toilet stalls with baby changing and menstrual hygiene management facilities, with a ratio of at least three female toilets for every two male toilets (2018 baseline: 0) OP2.1.4 Progress/Status: All new toilet facilities have toilet stalls for women and men in ratio of at least 2:1 and baby changing and menstrual hygiene management facilities. The new public toilet facilities have been well received by the Koror community. Data Source: PPUC certificate of completion Actual value:

Output: Safe and hygienic public toilet facilities in Koror are constructed Indicator: Three new gender-sensitive public toilet facilities constructed at the Koror shopping district, Koror tourist precinct, and Malakal recreation area, with a ratio of three female toilets for every two male toilets, and including menstrual hygiene facilities and roadside signage (2018 baseline: 0) OP2.1.4 Progress/Status: Two new gender sensitive toilet facilities have been constructed. Bidding for the construction of the third toilet facility (located P-Dock) is scheduled to commence in late-July 2026 and the works completed by 31 December 2026. Data Source: PPUC certificate of completion Actual value:

Output: Sewage treatment and disposal meet Palau's environmental standards Indicator: The BOD and the suspended solids concentrations of 95% of weekly plant effluent quality tests at the Malakal STP do not exceed 30 mg/l BOD and 30 mg/l suspended solids (2018 baseline: 40 mg/l and 40 mg/l suspended solids) OP3.3.2 Progress/Status: Effluent discharged from the Malakal WWTP is meeting the targets with more than 95% of samples meeting the compliance standards. Data Source: PPUC Malakal Waste Water Treatment Plant effluent water quality monitoring data Actual value:

Output: Effective, efficient, and sustainable sewage collection systems in Koror Indicator: Average monthly power consumption of Koror sewage pump stations per equivalent population at pump stations decreased by 10% (2018 baseline: 2.3 kWh/person) OP4.1.1 Progress/Status: I/I significantly increases sewer flows which are pumped to the Malakal WWTP increasing PPUC's sewer operations energy costs. When the project's new sewers are commissioned, I/I is expected to diminish and the volume of sewage pumped through the sewer systems reduced resulting in reduced pumping and lower power consumption per equivalent population at pump stations. Data Source: PPUC performance monitoring information Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: 2.3kWh Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: 2.3kWh Target year: 2027 Target value: 10%

Output: Effective, efficient, and sustainable sewage collection systems in Koror Indicator: Emergency callouts for pump station overflows decreased by 30% (2018 baseline: 25 callouts) OP4.1.1 Progress/Status: The number of emergency callouts for sewer pumping station overflows declined from 25 in 2018 to 7 in 2022 (more recent data is not available). Data Source: PPUC performance monitoring information Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: 25 callouts Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: 25 callouts Target year: 2027 Target value: <18 callouts

Output: Effective, efficient, and sustainable sewage collection systems in Koror Indicator: Response time to sewer system failures decreased to less than 2 hours (2018 baseline: 2.4 hours) OP4.1.1 Progress/Status: Response time to system failure decreased to less than 2 hours (2018 baseline: 2.4 hours), the latest available data (2019) indicates that PPUC is on track to meet the target. PPUC reporting on response time is structured for less than 3 hours, 3-6 hours, and greater than 6 hours. The response time and time for resolution for 9 of the 10 sewer pumping station overflow events that occurred in 2019 was less than 3 hours. One overflow event took approximately 6 hours to resolve. Data Source: PPUC performance monitoring information Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: 2.4 hours Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: 2.4 hours Target year: 2027 Target value: 2 hours
